title: [Forecast quý 2/2025] Tax collection in five countries
prompt: The table below gives information about the amount of tax collected ( as % of GDP) in five countries for 4 years between 1975 and 2005. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the proportion of tax revenue as a percentage of GDP collected in five countries over four decades from 1975 to 2005.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, most countries experienced an upward trend in tax collection rates during the given period, with Turkey showing initial decline before recovering. Sweden maintained the highest rates throughout and demonstrated the most significant growth, while the USA remained relatively stable.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with countries showing clear increases, Sweden collected 46% of GDP in taxes in 1975, more than three times higher than Japan's 15%. Sweden experienced dramatic growth, surging to 70.1% by 2005, an increase of over 24 percentage points. Japan followed a similar upward trajectory at a more moderate pace, rising gradually to 32.1% in the final year, more than doubling its initial rate.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining countries, the USA maintained stable figures throughout the period, starting at 25.1% in 1975 and ending at 27.4% in 2005, showing minimal variation of only 2.3 percentage points. Korea began at 15.1%, experienced a sharp rise to 27% by 1985, declined slightly to 26% in 1995, before recovering to 27.3% in 2005. Turkey showed the most irregular pattern, declining from 16.4% in 1975 to 15% in 1985, then recovering to 24% in 1995 and continuing to rise to 27.4% by 2005.
